title: Local SEO Audit: A 12-Step Checklist You Can Do Yourself
excerpt: A 12-step local SEO audit covering Google Business Profile, citations, reviews, website, links, competitors, tracking and AI search, with a checklist, worked example and report template.

meta.rl_answer: A local SEO audit checks how well your business appears in local results, Google Maps and AI answers. Check your Google Business Profile, citations, reviews, local keywords, website, local pack position, links, competitors, tracking, technical basics and AI search, then write a prioritized fix list and repeat it each year.
meta.rl_takeaways:
Run a full local SEO audit once a year and a short check each quarter.
Start with your Google Business Profile. For many local businesses it matters as much as the website.
Keep your name, address and phone number identical on every listing.
Reviews affect ranking and choice: ask every customer, reply to all, and never buy or write them.
Compare yourself with the three rivals that appear most often, and fill the gaps.
Sort fixes by impact and effort, then check again after 30 days.
Google says local results rest on relevance, distance and prominence, so each audit area feeds one of them.
meta.rl_faqs:
What is a local SEO audit? | A local SEO audit is a structured review of how well your business appears in local search, Google Maps and AI answers. It checks your Google Business Profile, listings, reviews, website, links and tracking, and ends with a prioritized list of fixes.
How do I do a local SEO audit? | Check your Google Business Profile, citations, reviews, local keywords, website pages, local pack position, links, competitors, tracking, technical basics and AI search results. Then write a fix list sorted by impact and effort.
How long does a local SEO audit take? | A small business with one location can finish a first pass in a day. Several locations or a large site can take a week or more. The fixes usually take longer than the audit.
How often should I run a local SEO audit? | Run a full audit once a year and a short check every quarter. Check sooner after a move, a rebrand, a new location or a drop in calls.
What tools do I need for a local SEO audit? | You can do a good first audit with free tools: Google Business Profile, Search Console, Analytics and PageSpeed Insights. Paid tools such as BrightLocal, Semrush or Moz Local save time with many locations.
What is NAP and why does it matter? | NAP is your business name, address and phone number. Search engines compare it across the web to confirm your business is real, so it should be identical everywhere.
How do I improve my local SEO after an audit? | Fix the high-impact, low-effort items first, such as wrong details, categories and a review request process. Then build service and location pages, grow reviews and earn honest local links, and check again after 30 days.
Do reviews affect local SEO? | Yes. Reviews are part of how Google judges how well known and trusted a business is, and they strongly affect whether a customer picks you. Ask every customer, reply to every review and never buy or write your own.
Is a local SEO audit different from a regular SEO audit? | Yes. A regular audit focuses on the website. A local audit adds your Google Business Profile, citations, reviews, local pack position and local links, which often matter more for searches tied to a place.
Can AI tools show my local business? | Yes, they can draw on your site, profile, reviews and listings. Check what they say about you, fix wrong details at the source and keep your facts consistent. No method guarantees a mention.

meta.rl_g_glossary:
NAP | Name, address and phone number. They should match everywhere online.
Citation | Any online mention of your business name, address and phone number, such as a directory listing.
Local pack | The box of three local businesses with a map that appears at the top of many local searches.
Google Business Profile | Your free listing in Google Search and Maps.
Schema markup | Code that tells search engines what a page is about, such as a local business and its address.
